definitions.E15:
I’ll keep **Specialty Nursing (Neonatal), Bachelor of Science in Nursing, Part-time** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science in Nursing  
- **School:** School of Health Sciences  
- **Study mode:** Part-time  
- **Delivery:** Fully online  
- **Status:** Active  
- **Total credits:** 60.0  
- **Stored program overview:** “The only neonatal certification program in Canada, BCIT’s Neonatal specialty nursing program is known in the health care industry for delivering quality e”  
  *The available program record ends at “quality e.”*

### Curriculum

**Required courses — 21 credits**
- **NSNE 7100 — Neonatal Theory 1** — 3 credits
- **NSNE 7200 — Neonatal Theory 2** — 3 credits
- **NSNE 7300 — Neonatal Clinical 1** — 4 credits
- **NSNE 7900 — Clinical Preceptorship in Neonatal Nursing** — 3 credits
- **NSNE 7911 — Neonatal Respiratory Care** — 4 credits
- **NSPN 7150 — The Breastfeeding Experience** — 3 credits
- **NSPN 7450 — Neonatal Resuscitation** — 1 credit

**Elective requirement**
Complete **at least 3 credits from the approved elective pool**. Electives must be approved by the Program Head:
- **NSNE 7920 — Neonatal Acute Care** — 4 credits
- **NSNE 7940 — Advanced Concepts in Neonatal Nursing** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 7000 — Palliative Approach in Nursing Practice** — 3 credits

The program record also identifies these possible sources for approved electives: ACORN through Perinatal Services BC, selected electives from the Pediatric Nursing Specialty Program, and selected electives from the Perinatal Nursing Specialty Program.

**Core/Management Component — 24 credits**
- **BUSA 7250 — Management Skills and Applications** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 7115 — Teaching and Learning in Specialty Nursing** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8000 — Systematic Inquiry** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8130 — Independent Study in Specialty Nursing** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8300 — Creative Leadership** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8500 — Professional Growth** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8600 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8800 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health Action** — 3 credits

**Liberal Studies Component — 12 credits**
- **COMM 7100 — Intercultural Communication Competency and Diversity Awareness for Professionals** — 3 credits
- **LIBS 7021 — Health Ethics** — 3 credits
- Plus **6 credits of General Education electives** at the 100-level minimum, from at least two academic disciplines.

### Published entrance requirements
The program record lists:
- English Studies 12 at **73%**, or equivalent
- A post-secondary diploma in nursing
- Current practicing RN registration or a Canadian provincial equivalent
- At least **six months of acute-care work experience**
- A resume of work experience

Clinical participation also involves registration confirmation, qualifying CPR certification, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization-or-masking policy. These requirements require institutional or program confirmation where indicated.

For international applicants, the record states that the program may be completed from outside Canada or by applicants with a valid Canadian work permit covering the clinical-training period. It also states that the program is **not eligible for a study permit** and is **not eligible for a PGWP**.

**Program source:** [BCIT Specialty Nursing (Neonatal), Bachelor of Science in Nursing](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

definitions.E1:
## Before applying: Specialty Nursing (Neonatal), Bachelor of Science in Nursing, Part-time

- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science in Nursing  
- **School:** School of Health Sciences  
- **Delivery:** Fully online, part-time  
- **Total:** 60 credits  
- **Status:** Active  

### Admission requirements

The stored admission requirements include:

- **English Studies 12 with at least 73%**, or equivalent
- A **post-secondary nursing diploma**
- Current practicing registration with the **BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM)**, a Canadian provincial equivalent, or an RN licence number if practising outside Canada
- At least **six months of acute-care work experience**
- A **resume of your work experience**

Registration, resume documentation, and whether your experience is equivalent or sufficiently recent require institutional or Program Head confirmation. Exceptions to the work-experience requirement may apply to some undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates.

### Clinical requirements

Although the program is delivered online, it includes clinical courses and placements. Before participating in clinical education, you should be prepared to provide or complete:

- Current qualifying **CPR certification** from a Canadian provider
- Proof of professional nursing registration
- Respirator fit testing
- Compliance with the influenza immunization-or-masking policy
- A clinical application

The available data does not specify an authoritative total number of clinical practice hours.

### International applicants

International applicants must either:

- Complete the program from outside Canada, or
- Have a valid Canadian work permit covering the duration of clinical training

The stored rules also state that:

- International applicants need **Program Head approval before applying**
- This program is **not eligible for a study permit**
- It is **not eligible for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)** under the stored program information

### Program structure

The curriculum totals 60 credits:

- **21 credits** of required neonatal courses
- **At least 3 credits from the approved elective pool**; electives must be approved by the Program Head
- **24 credits** in core and management studies
- **12 credits** in Liberal Studies, including 6 credits of required courses and 6 credits of general-education electives at the 100 level or higher in at least two academic disciplines

The listed courses include:

**Required neonatal courses**

- **NSNE 7100 — Neonatal Theory 1**
- **NSNE 7200 — Neonatal Theory 2**
- **NSNE 7300 — Neonatal Clinical 1**
- **NSNE 7900 — Clinical Preceptorship in Neonatal Nursing**
- **NSNE 7911 — Neonatal Respiratory Care**
- **NSPN 7150 — The Breastfeeding Experience**
- **NSPN 7450 — Neonatal Resuscitation**

**Approved elective pool**

You must complete **at least 3 credits from the approved pool**, rather than a fixed number of courses:

- **NSNE 7920 — Neonatal Acute Care**
- **NSNE 7940 — Advanced Concepts in Neonatal Nursing**
- **NSSC 7000 — Palliative Approach in Nursing Practice**

**Core and management courses**

- **BUSA 7250 — Management Skills and Applications**
- **NSSC 7115 — Teaching and Learning in Specialty Nursing**
- **NSSC 8000 — Systematic Inquiry**
- **NSSC 8130 — Independent Study in Specialty Nursing**
- **NSSC 8300 — Creative Leadership**
- **NSSC 8500 — Professional Growth**
- **NSSC 8600 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health**
- **NSSC 8800 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health Action**

**Required Liberal Studies courses**

- **COMM 7100 — Intercultural Communication Competency and Diversity Awareness for Professionals**
- **LIBS 7021 — Health Ethics**

### Application timing

The program has ongoing part-time intakes in **January, April, and September**. Applications are accepted throughout the year, but intakes may fill before the stated deadlines, so the stored information recommends applying early. Application timing and current availability should be confirmed with BCIT because the available record contains intake dates that may change.

[View the program information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

- **Current professional registration:** proof of practicing RN registration or an equivalent licence.
- **Acute-care experience:** whether your experience is equivalent and sufficiently recent. A refresher course may be required if the experience is not recent.
- **Resume and placement documentation:** acceptance and suitability of the submitted documents.
- **Program Head approval:** required for international applicants before applying.
- **International eligibility:** whether your program location or Canadian work permit covers the entire period of clinical training.
- **Clinical requirements:**
  - Current qualifying CPR certification with a practical component.
  - Respirator fit-testing evidence and renewal requirements.
  - Compliance with the influenza-immunization-or-masking policy.
  - Clinical placement documentation.
- **Clinical practice hours:** clinical participation is required, but the available record does not state an authoritative numeric hour requirement.
- **Transfer credit or prior-learning assessment:** these are assessed individually by the appropriate BCIT office or program faculty.
- **Admission discretion and availability:** meeting the published requirements does not guarantee admission; the Program Head may enforce or waive requirements, and intakes may fill before deadlines.

The program record also indicates that application dates and availability can change. Confirm current details directly with BCIT: [program information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/).

definitions.E10:
For the **Applied Computing, Master of Science**, admission is competitive and has two steps.

### Step 1: Meet the entrance requirements

All applicants need:

- **English proficiency:** Graduate Studies English Studies 12 with at least **67%**, or an equivalent qualification.
- **One of these entry routes:**
  1. **Standard entry:** A bachelor’s degree in computer science or an equivalent field, with a minimum **2.8/4.0 GPA (70%)** based on the final 30 undergraduate credits.
  2. **Alternate entry:** A bachelor’s degree in another discipline, with a minimum **3.0/4.0 GPA (73%)** based on the final 30 credits, plus significant computing knowledge through formal education and/or work experience. A pre-entry assessment and possible bridging courses may be required.

Alternate-entry applicants must also complete the **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire**. It requires **two references**, whose forms must be sent directly to the M.Sc. admissions committee.

Applicants with post-secondary studies completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand require a comprehensive **ICES credential evaluation**; other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.

### Step 2: Department review

Complete applications are reviewed and ranked competitively by the Graduate Program Committee. Relevant industry experience is preferred but is not listed as a minimum requirement.

Applicants currently in the final term of their degree must be on track to graduate by July before the intake begins and may be conditionally accepted based on successful completion.

### Application timing

The program has a September intake:

- First round: October 1–January 31  
- Second round: February 1–March 31  
- Third round: April 1–June 15  
- International applicants need a valid BCIT study permit to apply in the third round.
- The **September 2026 intake is closed**. Applications for **September 2027** are scheduled to open **October 1, 2026**.

For international applicants, a valid BCIT study permit is required before starting the program. The program record does not provide a guaranteed admission outcome; final selection depends on the competitive department review.

[Program admission information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/applied-computing-master-of-science-full-time-m600msc/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

definitions.E25: The Master of Science Degree in Applied Computing gives you in-depth computing knowledge to solve complex real-world problems across industries and sectors. Through an interdisciplinary and rigorous full-time curriculum, you’ll be equipped to provide technical leadership in a professional setting or pursue further academic study. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing About the program Applied computing integrates information technology, computer science, and industry. You’ll take courses in core computing, and you will have the opportunity to work in an application area in another discipline. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how advanced computing, tools, and computational methods can be applied in practice to overcome challenges and create efficiencies. The program employs a cohort model, with the same group in all courses. This allows you to work through the program together, sharing your experience and expertise and building industry connections that will last long after you graduate 1 intake: September 4 15-week terms, normally completed over two academic years full time First year with two terms , delivered in-person, including: Algorithm analysis Human-centered Computing Machine Learning (ML) & Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Science Cybersecurity Research methods Second year on thesis path or internship & project path Based on BCIT Burnaby Campus, and possibly the Downtown Campus or field locations where appropriate. You’ll be uniquely qualified to apply your knowledge and skills in various areas, such as: computational science rehabilitation engineering building science biotechnology autonomous vehicles sustainability smart micro-grids social impacts of technology network security an approved project area of your choosing based on your professional background See the Program Details to learn more. Who it’s for This degree might be for you if you: Are inspired to maximize the societal benefit of computing by solving real-world issues Would like to apply your skills in industry after graduation, but might also consider applying for a PhD Are looking for a cohort-based program where you’ll work with other students to share problem-solving skills and approaches, as you would in a work setting Have an applied problem you believe could be improved through computing Would like to study with computing faculty, application experts outside of computing, and industry partners Students will also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to gain additional knowledge in a specific application area. Please review the Entrance Requirements to learn more. What grads can do Provide technical leadership for software/system development teams Demonstrate deep, critical knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in computing science Analyze how computing systems and software can be used in practical applications and interdisciplinary fields Design, develop, and implement innovative solutions to industry problems with consideration to relevant ethical, social and environmental issues Explain and advocate for applied computing solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences in both business and academic settings See the Graduating & Jobs page to learn more. definitions.E27: This degree focuses on Applied Computing, which is fundamentally related to applying computing technology and computational methods to derive solutions to complex practical problems. Course work will emphasize current issues in industry, case studies, and applied research projects. This program offers you a chance to work with an interdisciplinary and diverse team of academic supervisors that may include faculty from Computing, faculty from an application domain, as well as industry practitioners. You’ll also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to explore a specific application area. For more information about faculty, visit the Faculty, Advisors & Staff page. Applied research is fundamental to the program. Two paths are offered, diverging in second year: Thesis Path – Path 1: complete a thesis project and defend it in your second year. You’ll need to demonstrate originality in the application of your knowledge, either through new publishable research, or a novel solution to an existing practical problem. This is the best path if you’re interested in possibly pursuing a future Ph.D. Project & Internship Path – Path 2: a one-semester research project with a one-semester internship, which may be paid or unpaid. The internship will involve an external company or a BCIT lab where you can learn how advanced computing techniques are applied to solve interdisciplinary problems. The research project may be done in collaboration with the sponsor from the internship, providing added value in terms of practical utility. Students will also complete a 3-credit special topics course, covering emerging areas in Applied Computing, such as Quantum Computing, Generative AI, or Deep Learning. Both paths will require students to: examine literature in a related discipline, recognize gaps and limitations in existing technologies and processes, organize and plan their approach, and demonstrate competence in applying advanced techniques to solve problems. In both paths, students will present a written argument that addresses a complex problem in applied computing. Did you miss our Info Session? Please see the recording from October 2024: BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing | Info Session Program length Two years, full-time. The maximum time to complete this program is five years. Grading Students will be required to maintain a minimum average of 70% across all courses in the program before starting their thesis or research project. Student progress through the program will be monitored by the supervisor, in consultation with the Program Head. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs

definitions.E3: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements The following are requirements for entry into Specialty Nursing certificate and degree courses. Enforcement or waiving of any or all entry requirements is at the discretion of the program head. If you have any questions about your experience or qualifications, please contact the program head. English language proficiency: Category 1 – English Studies 12 (73%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma in nursing Current practicing registration with one of the following: BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) or Canadian provincial equivalent or Registered Nurse (RN) license number (if practicing outside Canada) Work Experience: minimum six months work experience in an acute care setting Submit a resume of work experience with your application. Exceptions may be granted for undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates. A resume is required for placement in the program. If you have questions about whether your work experience qualifies, please contact the program head. Interested nurses from international practice, residential, or other areas of care lacking recent (within two years) acute care experience may be required to complete a refresher course. BCIT recommends the following programs: Douglas College Kwantlen Polytechnic University Thompson Rivers University Please contact one of the institutions above, as well as the program head, to determine an appropriate preparatory course of study. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Clinical requirements Note: Effective immediately, all healthcare workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded healthcare facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, will have to get the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification All students participating in clinical courses must have current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Level C or Level Health Care Provider (HCP). CPR certification must be from a Canadian provider and include a practical component. The original certificate must be presented upon application to clinical courses. BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) registration As well as providing this information at the time of admission, BCIT requires students to provide proof of BCCNM membership, Canadian provincial equivalent, or RN license number for each clinical course. Without proper registration, you will not be permitted to continue in the course. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test is required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose.
